title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Cambodia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a Cambodian citizen living in Cambodia is preparing medical, legal, and financial administration while facing a serious or life-limiting illness, acting before mental capacity is impaired avoids court guardianship delays and protects family access to funds and records. Because Cambodian ministries maintain limited English-language procedural portals online and publish domestic regulations primarily in Khmer, this planning guide draws on verified statutory texts in international legal archives (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, and UNESCAP CRVS) alongside official Cambodian portals such as National Social Security Fund (NSSF), Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC), and Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) Cambodia [1][2][4][5].

steps.title: Healthcare access, palliative coordination, and insurance records
steps.html:
• National Social Security Fund (NSSF) health care scheme: Verify active NSSF Health Care Scheme registration (for private-sector workers, civil servants, or voluntary contributors) alongside IDPoor/Health Equity Fund or private medical insurance cards so inpatient hospital and specialist clinic visits remain covered [2][3][7].
  • Hospital care and home-care planning: Coordinate pain relief, palliative support, and home-nursing referrals directly with treating specialists at national or provincial referral hospitals, as dedicated community hospice networks outside Phnom Penh remain limited [2][7].
  • Consolidate medical files: Maintain organized copies of diagnostic summaries, medication schedules, Khmer National ID, and Family Book records for clinic admissions and disability benefit reviews [7].

steps.title: Medical consent and advance care conversations
steps.html:
• Absence of a standalone living-will statute: Cambodia does not have a dedicated statutory Advance Medical Directive or Lasting Healthcare Power of Attorney law, so treatment preferences rely on family consent and direct medical-team communication [1].
  • Recording treatment wishes in hospital notes: While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, document clear wishes on resuscitation, intensive care, and home vs. hospital care with the attending physicians and name the trusted family spokesperson in clinical charts [1][8].
  • Emergency contact clarity: Share signed copies of those clinical preferences and the emergency family spokesperson's contact details with close relatives to avoid conflicting bedside decisions [1].

steps.title: Financial mandates, agency limits, and Civil Code guardianship
steps.html:
• Mandate contracts and bank delegations: Under Book IV (Obligations/Mandate) of the Civil Code of Cambodia, your family member can grant notarized mandates or bank-specific signing authorities while retaining capacity to manage bills, salaries, and property upkeep [1].
  • Ordinary mandate limitations upon incapacity: Because Cambodia has no standalone statutory Lasting Power of Attorney framework, an ordinary mandate can become ineffective or restricted if the grantor loses mental capacity, meaning early arrangement of accessible household bill-payment funds is important [1].
  • Court guardianship and curatorship fallback: Under Book VII (Relatives) of the Civil Code of Cambodia and the Code of Civil Procedure tracked on ILO NATLEX, once an adult lacks decision-making capacity, relatives must petition the provincial/municipal Court of First Instance to declare legal incapacity (guardianship or curatorship) and appoint a legal guardian or curator [1][9].

steps.title: Social security incapacity pensions and caregiver arrangements
steps.html:
• NSSF Invalidity / Incapacity Pension: Under the Law on Social Security Schemes (Royal Kram No. NS/RKM/1119/018) indexed by Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC) and published on FAOLEX, insured members of National Social Security Fund (NSSF) who suffer permanent physical or mental incapacity preventing gainful work may claim an Invalidity Pension (or occupational disability pension if work-related) subject to medical assessment and contribution conditions [2][3][4][7].
  • Sickness and workplace leave benefits: Employed contributors should apply for NSSF sickness allowances and document extended medical leave with employers using certified medical reports [2][7].
  • Collect contribution records early: Obtain updated contribution statements through NSSF member portals or local NSSF offices so pension, invalidity, and health eligibility are verified without delay [3][7].

steps.title: Wills, property titles, and cross-border legalization
steps.html:
• Executing a formal will under Book VIII: Under Book VIII (Succession) of the Civil Code of Cambodia, your family member can execute a notarial will (before a Cambodian notary public), a handwritten holographic will, or a secret will; confirm that any will respects statutory legally secured portions for qualifying spouse, children, and parents [1].
  • Auditing civil documents and land titles: Verify accuracy across the Khmer National ID, Family Book (Siev Phov Krousar), birth and marriage certificates managed through the Commune or Sangkat Office, and land titles (distinguishing registered Ministry of Land Management hard titles from commune-level soft titles) [1][5][6].
  • Consular legalization for foreign use: Because Cambodia is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, notarized documents or powers intended for use abroad must undergo translation and consular authentication through Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) Cambodia and the destination country's embassy [6][10].
